chunks: Then he (peace be upon him) said: O people,

I have divulged to you the advice which the prophets used to preach to their peoples, and I have conveyed to you what the vicegerents conveyed to those coming after them. I tried to train you with my whip but you could not be straightened, and I drove you with admonition but you did not acquire proper behaviour.
May Allah deal with you! Do you expect an Imam other than me to take you on the path, and show you the way?
ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about his efforts to guide the people and their response?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) reflects on his comprehensive leadership, asserting that he delivered the prophetic message and applied the disciplinary measures of the Imams, yet the people remained unresponsive to both gentle advice and firm correction. This highlights the Shia concept of the Imam as the perfect guide who fulfills all roles of teaching, disciplining, and directing, making his authority sufficient for guidance. The rhetorical question challenges the community's reliance on external leadership while neglecting the established, divinely appointed Imam.
